\begin{definition}[Predictable Subspace and Conditional-Expectation
Operator]\label{def:predictable}
$H_X^{\mathcal{P}} \subseteq H_X$ is the closed subspace of
predictable processes (i.e., processes measurable with respect to the
predictable $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{P}$ on
$[0,T] \times \Omega$).  We say $H_X$ admits a
\emph{conditional-expectation operator} if there exists a bounded
linear projection $\Pi_X : H_X \to H_X^{\mathcal{P}}$ satisfying:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Idempotence:} $\Pi_X^2 = \Pi_X$ and
  $\Pi_X|_{H_X^{\mathcal{P}}} = \Id$.
\item \textbf{Pointwise representation:}
  $(\Pi_X u)_t = \E[u_t \mid \mathcal{F}_{t-}]$ for $t \in (0,T]$
  and $(\Pi_X u)_0 = \E[u_0 \mid \mathcal{F}_0]$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

title: Banach adjoint derivative
extraction: mechanical declaration index, not a proof certificate
statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Banach adjoint derivative]
\label{def:derivative}
Let $\delta_X : H_X \to L^p(\Omega)$ be a bounded stochastic
integral (Definition~\ref{def:integrand-space}).  The
\emph{Banach adjoint derivative} is the dual operator
\[
  D_X := \delta_X^* : L^q(\Omega) \to H_X^*,
\]
defined by the duality pairing
\begin{equation}\label{eq:DX-def}
  \langle D_X F, u \rangle_{H_X^*, H_X}
  := \E\bigl[F \cdot \delta_X(u)\bigr]
  \qquad \text{for all } F \in L^q(\Omega),\; u \in H_X.
\end{equation}
This is well-defined and bounded: by H\"older's inequality,
$|\E[F \cdot \delta_X(u)]| \leq \|F\|_q\,\|\delta_X(u)\|_p
\leq \|F\|_q\,C_\delta\,\|u\|_{H_X}$,
so $D_X F \in H_X^*$ with $\|D_X F\|_{H_X^*} \leq C_\delta\,\|F\|_q$.
\end{definition}

statement_tex:
\begin{assumption}[Factorization Hypotheses]\label{ass:factorization}
Let $X$ be a process with integrand space $H_X$, stochastic integral
$\delta_X : H_X \to L^p(\Omega)$, conditional-expectation operator
$\Pi_X$ (Definition~\ref{def:predictable}), predictable subspace
$H_X^{\mathcal{P}} \subseteq H_X$, and Banach adjoint derivative
$D_X = \delta_X^* : L^q(\Omega) \to H_X^*$.  We assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)}]
\item \label{H:centered} \textup{Centered integrals:}
  $\E[\delta_X(u)] = 0$ for all $u \in H_X$.
\item \label{H:injective} \textup{Injectivity on predictable
  integrands:} The restriction
  $\delta_X|_{H_X^{\mathcal{P}}} : H_X^{\mathcal{P}} \to L^p(\Omega)$
  is injective.
\item \label{H:representation} \textup{Representation property:}
  Every $\mathcal{F}_T^X$-measurable
  $\tilde{F} \in L^p(\Omega) \cap L^q(\Omega)$ with
  $\E[\tilde{F}] = 0$ can be written as
  $\tilde{F} = \delta_X(v)$ for some predictable
  $v \in H_X^{\mathcal{P}}$.
\item \label{H:Pi} \textup{Bounded conditional expectation:}
  $\Pi_X$ satisfies Definition~\ref{def:predictable}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{assumption}

title: Fluctuation Factorization (Theorem~A)
extraction: mechanical declaration index, not a proof certificate
statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Fluctuation Factorization (Theorem~A)]
\label{thm:factorization}
Let $\delta_X : H_X \to L^p(\Omega)$ be a bounded stochastic integral
satisfying hypotheses \textup{(H1)}--\textup{(H4)} of
Assumption~\ref{ass:factorization}.  Then for all
$\mathcal{F}_T^X$-measurable $F \in L^p(\Omega) \cap L^q(\Omega)$:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:factorization-thm}
  F - \E[F] = \delta_X\bigl(\delta_X^{-1}(F - \E[F])\bigr),
\end{equation}
where $\delta_X^{-1}$ is the recovery map of
Remark~\textup{\ref{rem:recovery}}.  More informatively,
the unique representing integrand
$v = \delta_X^{-1}(F - \E[F]) \in H_X^{\mathcal{P}}$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:duality-recovery}
  \langle D_X F, u \rangle = \E[\delta_X(v) \cdot \delta_X(u)]
  \qquad \text{for all } u \in H_X^{\mathcal{P}},
\end{equation}
whenever the product on the right is integrable.
Equivalently, as an operator identity on
$L^p(\Omega, \mathcal{F}_T^X) \cap L^q(\Omega, \mathcal{F}_T^X)$:
\[
  \Id - \E = \delta_X \circ \delta_X^{-1} \circ (\Id - \E).
\]
\end{theorem}

title: Stable Integrand Space
extraction: mechanical declaration index, not a proof certificate
statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Stable Integrand Space]\label{def:HL}
Fix $p \in (1,\gamma)$.  Let $H_L$ be the Banach space of
predictable processes $u : [0,T] \times \Omega \to \R$ with
\[
  \|u\|_{H_L} :=
  \left(\E\!\left[\left(\int_0^T |u_t|^\gamma\,dt\right)^{p/\gamma}\,\right]\right)^{\!1/p}
  < \infty,
\]
i.e., the closed predictable subspace of the Bochner space
$L^p\bigl(\Omega; L^\gamma([0,T], dt)\bigr)$.  The norm
$\|\cdot\|_{H_L}$ is the natural \emph{stable scale}: for
deterministic $u$ it reduces to the $\gamma$-stable scale
parameter $\bigl(\int_0^T |u_t|^\gamma\,dt\bigr)^{1/\gamma}$, which
governs $\int u_t\,dL_t$ as a $\gamma$-stable random variable
(\cite{Sato1999}, Prop.~14.5).

The stochastic integral $\delta_L : H_L \to L^p(\Omega)$ is defined
by
\[
  \delta_L(u) := \int_0^T \!\!\int_{\R \setminus \{0\}}
  u_t\,z\,\widetilde{N}(dt,dz) = \int_0^T u_t\,dL_t,
\]
initially for simple predictable $u$ and extended by continuity.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Deterministic baseline.}
For deterministic $u \in L^\gamma([0,T], dt)$, the symmetric
$\gamma$-stable scaling identity
\[
  \|\delta_L(u)\|_{L^p}
  \;=\; c_{p,\gamma}\,
  \Bigl(\int_0^T |u_t|^\gamma\,dt\Bigr)^{\!1/\gamma}
  \qquad (\text{deterministic } u)
\]
holds with a finite constant $c_{p,\gamma} > 0$ depending only on
$p$ and $\gamma$ (\cite{Sato1999}, Prop.~14.5;
\cite{Applebaum2009}, \S4.4; \cite{MarcusRosinski2005}).

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Upper bound for predictable integrands.}
For random predictable $u \in H_L$, the Bichteler--Jacod /
Marinelli--R\"ockner inequality on the stable scale yields
$\|\delta_L(u)\|_{L^p} \leq C_{p,\gamma}\,\|u\|_{H_L}$ with a
finite $C_{p,\gamma}$ depending only on $p$ and $\gamma$
(\cite{BichtelerJacod1983, MarinelliRoeckner2014, Dirksen2014};
see also \cite{Applebaum2009}, Thm.~4.4.23).

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Two-sided extension.}
The reverse inequality on the predictable stable scale is more
delicate (the deterministic argument does not transfer
verbatim).  We adopt the two-sided version as a standing
assumption (Assumption~\ref{ass:stable-scale} below).

\medskip
The naive choice $H_L = L^p([0,T] \times \Omega, dt \otimes dP)$ is
\emph{not} the right scale for stable integrals: for deterministic
$u = \mathbf{1}_{[0,T_0]}$,
$\|\delta_L(u)\|_{L^p} = \|L_{T_0}\|_{L^p} \asymp T_0^{1/\gamma}$
while $\bigl(\int_0^T|u|^p\,dt\bigr)^{1/p} = T_0^{1/p}$, and these
scale differently in $T_0$ since $1/\gamma < 1/p$.  Replacing the
inner time exponent by $\gamma$ matches the stable scale and
restores the two-sided $L^p$-isomorphism (under
Assumption~\ref{ass:stable-scale}).  The structural obstruction to
a $p$-homogeneous norm with a full Burkholder--Rosenthal-type
equivalence \emph{containing the stable identity integrand $z$} in
the two-parameter setting is analyzed in the
companion~\cite{Fontes2026e}.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[No Riesz Representor]\label{prop:no-riesz}
Since $p \in (1,\gamma)$ with $\gamma < 2$, both $p$ and $\gamma$
lie in $(1,2)$.  $H_L$ is a closed subspace of the Bochner space
$L^p(\Omega; L^\gamma([0,T]))$, hence has type $\min(p, \gamma)$
and cotype $2$, with $\min(p,\gamma) < 2$.  By Kwapie\'n's theorem,
$H_L$ is not isomorphic to any Hilbert space, and in particular not
to its dual $H_L^*$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{definition}[Truncated integral]\label{def:truncated}
For $M > 0$, define $z_M := z\,\mathbf{1}_{|z| \leq M}$ and
\[
  \delta_L^M(u) := I_1(u \cdot z_M)
  = \int_0^T\!\!\int_{|z| \leq M} u(s)\,z\,\widetilde{N}(ds,dz).
\]
Since $\int_{|z| \leq M} z^2\,\nu_\gamma(dz) < \infty$, the
integrand $u \cdot z_M \in L^2(dt \otimes \nu_\gamma)$ for all
$u \in L^2([0,T])$, and the $L^2$-isometry applies to $\delta_L^M$.
\end{definition}

statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Chaos Characterization]\label{thm:chaos}
Let $L$ be a symmetric $\gamma$-stable process with
$\gamma \in (1,2)$, and let $F \in L^2(\Omega, \mathcal{F}_T^L)$
with Poisson chaos expansion $F = \sum_{n \geq 0} I_n(f_n)$.
Write $H_L^{\mathrm{det}} := L^\gamma([0,T], dt) \subset H_L$ for
the closed subspace of deterministic integrands; recall that
$\|u\|_{H_L} = (\int_0^T |u|^\gamma\,dt)^{1/\gamma}$ for
deterministic $u$ (Definition~\ref{def:HL}).
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \textup{(Deterministic kernel.)}
  $\E[F \cdot \delta_L(u)] = 0$ for all deterministic
  $u \in H_L^{\mathrm{det}}$ if and only if the first chaos kernel
  $f_1$ of $F$ satisfies
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:kernel-char}
    \Phi_M(s) := \int_{|z| \leq M}
    f_1(s,z)\,z\,\nu_\gamma(dz) \;\longrightarrow\; 0
    \quad \text{in } L^{\gamma'}([0,T], dt) \text{ as } M \to \infty,
  \end{equation}
  where $\gamma' = \gamma/(\gamma-1)$ is the conjugate of $\gamma$.
  In particular, the deterministic annihilator
  $\{F \in L^q_0 : \E[F \cdot \delta_L(u)] = 0\;
  \forall\,u \in H_L^{\mathrm{det}}\}$
  contains all constants, the entire higher chaos
  $\bigoplus_{n \geq 2} \mathcal{C}_n$, and all first-chaos
  elements with even kernels.

\item \textup{(Range.)}
  $\im(\delta_L)$ is a closed subspace of $L^p_0(\Omega)$
  (Proposition~\textup{\ref{prop:hypotheses}}).
  Every element of $\im(\delta_L)$ is a first-chaos element
  (in the sense that $\delta_L(u)$ is the $L^p$-limit
  of $I_1(u \cdot z_M)$ as $M \to \infty$), so
  $\im(\delta_L) \subseteq \mathcal{C}_1 \cap L^p$.  This
  inclusion is strict: the centered large-jump count
  $N_T - \E[N_T] = I_1(\mathbf{1}_{|z|>1})$ is in
  $\mathcal{C}_1 \cap L^r$ for all $r$ but not in
  $\im(\delta_L)$ (since it lies in the deterministic
  annihilator by~(i), as $\mathbf{1}_{|z|>1}$ is even).

\item \textup{(Infinite-dimensional annihilator.)}
  The deterministic annihilator is infinite-dimensional.
  The first-chaos elements $I_1(h_k)$ with
  $h_k(s,z) := \mathbf{1}_{[0,T]}(s)\,
  \mathbf{1}_{k < |z| \leq k+1}$ for $k = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$ are
  linearly independent (disjoint supports in $z$), lie in
  $L^r(\Omega)$ for all $r$ (each $h_k \in L^2(dt \otimes
  \nu_\gamma)$ since $\nu_\gamma(\{k < |z| \leq k+1\}) < \infty$),
  and satisfy \eqref{eq:kernel-char} (even kernels).  Hence the
  annihilator contains an infinite-dimensional subspace even within
  $\mathcal{C}_1$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product Rule with Jump Defect (Theorem~B)]
\label{thm:product-rule}
Let $f, g \in C_b^2(\R)$, $F = f(L_T)$, $G = g(L_T)$.
For bounded predictable $u \in H_L$, define
\begin{align*}
  L(F,G; u)
  &:= \E\!\left[\int_0^T f'(L_{t-})g(L_{t-})\,dL_t \cdot
  \delta_L(u)\right]\\
  &\quad+ \E\!\left[\int_0^T f(L_{t-})g'(L_{t-})\,dL_t \cdot
  \delta_L(u)\right],
\end{align*}
and
$\langle \Gamma_L(F,G), u \rangle := \langle D_L(FG), u \rangle
- L(F,G; u)$.
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:defect-formula}
  \langle \Gamma_L(F,G), u \rangle
  = \E\!\left[\sum_{0 < s \leq T} \Delta_s(f,g) \cdot
  \delta_L(u)\right],
\end{equation}
where the product jump defect is
\[
  \Delta_s(f,g) := (fg)(L_s) - (fg)(L_{s-})
  - [f'g + fg'](L_{s-})\,\Delta L_s.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:curvature}
On the space $\mathcal{T}_N^+ = \{f = \sum_{n=1}^N a_n\,e^{inx} :
a_n \in \C\}$ of positive-frequency trigonometric
polynomials, the Bakry--\'Emery
curvature is exactly
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kappa-def}
  \kappa(\gamma,N) = \lambda_{\min}\!\bigl(R_H^{\circ 2}, R_H\bigr),
  \qquad H = \gamma/2,
\end{equation}
where $R_H$ is the $N \times N$ fBM covariance matrix on $\{1,\ldots,N\}$.
Since $\mathcal{T} = \bigcup_N \mathcal{T}_N$ is a core for $L_\gamma$,
the curvature on the full domain satisfies
$\kappa(\gamma) \leq \lim_{N\to\infty} \kappa(\gamma,N)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Higher iterated carr\'e du champ]
\label{def:higher-gamma}
Define the sesquilinear operators $\Gamma_k$ inductively by
$\Gamma_1 := \widetilde{\Gamma}_\gamma$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Gammak-def}
  \Gamma_{k+1}(f,g)
  := \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl[
    L_\gamma\,\Gamma_k(f,g)
    - \Gamma_k(L_\gamma f, g)
    - \Gamma_k(f, L_\gamma g)
  \bigr],
  \qquad k \geq 1.
\end{equation}
The $k$-th order Bakry--\'Emery condition is
$\Gamma_k(f,f) \geq \kappa^{(k)}\,\Gamma_{k-1}(f,f)$.
\end{definition}

\label{thm:regularization}
For all $\gamma \in (0,2)$ and $N \geq 1$:

  it is the worst-case correlation between distinct

statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Iterated spectral inequality]
\label{prop:iterated}
For all $k \geq 1$:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:iterated}
  \kappa^{(k)}(\gamma,N)\,\mathcal{E}_{k-1}(f)
  \;\leq\; \mathcal{E}_k(f)
  \;\leq\; K^{(k)}(\gamma,N)\,\mathcal{E}_{k-1}(f),
\end{equation}
where
$\kappa^{(k)} = \lambda_{\min}(R_H^{\circ k}, R_H^{\circ(k-1)})$
and
$K^{(k)} = \lambda_{\max}(R_H^{\circ k}, R_H^{\circ(k-1)})$.
Iterating the lower bound:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:chain}
  \mathcal{E}_k(f)
  \;\geq\; \Bigl(\prod_{j=2}^k \kappa^{(j)}\Bigr)
  \cdot \mathcal{E}_1(f).
\end{equation}
At $\gamma = 1$:
$\prod_{j=2}^k \kappa_1^{(j)} = 1$ (the chain is sharp
at the first mode) and
$\prod_{j=2}^k K^{(j)} = \prod_{j=2}^k (2N-1)(3N^2-3N+1)
\cdots \to \infty$ (the maximum grows polynomially in $N$
at each step).
\end{proposition}

statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Global curvature under drift]\label{thm:global-drift}
At $\gamma = 1$, the Hermitianized drift correction satisfies
the scalar identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:drift-scalar}
  \Gamma_{L,2}(f,f)(x) - \Gamma_{1,2}(f,f)(x)
  = \frac{\omega^2}{2}\cos(x)\;\Gamma(f,f)(x)
\end{equation}
for all $f \in \mathcal{T}_N^+$ and all $x \in \T$.
Consequently, the eigenvalues of the curvature operator
$\Gamma^{-1}\Gamma_{L,2}$ on $\mathcal{T}_N^+$ are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:drift-eigenvalues}
  \kappa_k(x) = (2k-1) + \frac{\omega^2}{2}\cos x,
  \qquad k = 1,\ldots,N,
\end{equation}
and the global Bakry--\'Emery curvature is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:global-kappa}
  \kappa(1,\omega^2) = 1 - \frac{\omega^2}{2},
\end{equation}
independent of $N$, achieved at $x = \pi$.
Combined with the cross-sign vanishing
(Corollary~\ref{cor:block-diag}), this extends to all real
trigonometric polynomials.

In particular, $\mathrm{CD}(1-\omega^2/2,\,\infty)$ holds for
$\omega^2 < 2$, with consequences:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Poincar\'e inequality:
  $\Var_\mu(f) \leq \frac{1}{1-\omega^2/2}\,\mathcal{E}_L(f,f)$.
\item Gradient estimate:
  $\Gamma(P_t^L f, P_t^L f)
  \leq e^{-2(1-\omega^2/2)t}\,P_t^L[\Gamma(f,f)]$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[The tower is totally nonnegative]\label{prop:TN}
At the Cauchy point, for every real $j>0$ the chaos covariance
$R^{\Had j}=\min(n,m)^j$ is \emph{totally nonnegative}: every minor is
$\ge0$. Indeed $R^{\Had j}=LD_jL^{\top}$ is a product of totally
nonnegative matrices---$L$ and $L^{\top}$ have all minors in $\{0,1\}$,
$D_j$ is a positive diagonal---so total nonnegativity follows from the
Cauchy--Binet formula, which moreover evaluates each minor explicitly:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:CB}
   \det R^{\Had j}[I\,|\,J]
   =\sum_{K}\det L[I|K]\Bigl(\textstyle\prod_{k\in K}(k^j-(k-1)^j)\Bigr)
     \det L[J|K],
\end{equation}
a nonnegative sum of products of curvature eigenvalues, with leading
principal minors $\det R^{\Had j}[\{1,\dots,p\}]=\prod_{k\le p}(k^j-(k-1)^j)$.
This is once more the Cauchy point alone: for $H\neq\tfrac12$ the matrix
$R_H^{\Had2}$ already carries strictly negative minors (numerically, of
order $10$ to $10^2$ at $H=0.3,\dots,0.7$).

contained in $t\lesssim t_{**}=157$, with re-coherence governed by the
$x$-independent saddle detachment of $g(u)=tu^4+\log\Phi(u)$ at
$u_*=\tfrac34$, $t_*=\tfrac{64}{27}\pi e^3$. Hence $\Lambda(4)\approx155$ is
finite. The statement is numerics-plus-saddle: double precision resolves
the arithmetic only while $C(t)\lesssim30$ ($t\lesssim185$); beyond that
the saddle dominance, not the arithmetic, carries real-rootedness.
\end{proposition}

title: Critical-line zeros of the secular polynomial
extraction: mechanical declaration index, not a proof certificate
statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Critical-line zeros of the secular polynomial]
\label{prop:critline}
Write $M^{(j)}=p_j(\mathcal N+1)$ with secular polynomial
$p_j(z)=z^j-(z-1)^j$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:numberop}). Then $p_j$ has
degree $j-1$ and \emph{all its zeros lie on the critical line}
$\Re z=\tfrac12$, namely $z_r=\tfrac12+\tfrac{i}{2}\cot\frac{\pi r}{j}$,
$r=1,\dots,j-1$. Equivalently the rotation $z=\tfrac12+iw$ makes
$q_j(w):=p_j(\tfrac12+iw)$ hyperbolic (real-rooted), $q_j\in\LP$. The
curvature eigenvalues are its values on the number spectrum,
\[
   k^j-(k-1)^j=p_j(k)=j\prod_{r=1}^{j-1}(k-z_r),
\]
positive for every integer $k\ge1$ because the spectrum of $\mathcal N+1$
lies to the right of the zero-line and the $z_r$ occur in conjugate pairs;
the vacuum value $\kappa_j=p_j(1)=1$ is the value at the integer nearest
the line.
\end{proposition}

title: $\zeta$ as the curvature spectral zeta
extraction: mechanical declaration index, not a proof certificate
statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[$\zeta$ as the curvature spectral zeta]\label{prop:czeta}
At the Cauchy point the Bakry--\'Emery curvature operator
$M^{(2)}=2\mathcal N+1$ has spectrum the odd integers, so its spectral zeta
is
\[
   Z_2(s):=\sum_{k\ge1}(2k-1)^{-s}=(1-2^{-s})\,\zeta(s),
\]
the Dirichlet $\lambda$-function. In the critical strip its zeros coincide
with the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$; hence the Riemann hypothesis is
exactly the statement that the critical zeros of the curvature spectral
zeta lie on $\Re s=\tfrac12$. Its zeta-regularized determinant is
$\exp(-Z_2'(0))=\sqrt2$.
\end{proposition}

statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[B: pure-clock sector and expectation limit]
\label{thm:pure-clock}
For every $f\in\mathscr S(\R)$, $t\ge 0$, $\varepsilon>0$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Scalar identity)
\[
 \Pir_0^X\,C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)
 \;=\;F_\varepsilon(Y;t)
 \;\coloneqq\;\tfrac12\!\int_0^t\!\psi_\varepsilon(|Y_s|)\,ds,
\]
with $\psi_\varepsilon=\phi_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{int}}+b_\varepsilon$
as in \eqref{eq:phi-int-def}--\eqref{eq:b-eps}.
\item (Bidegree slices) For every $n\ge 0$,
\[
 \Pir_{0,n}\,C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)
 \;=\;\Pir_n^Y F_\varepsilon(Y;t).
\]
\item (Expectation limit)
\[
 \Pir_{0,0}\,C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)
 \;=\;\E\!\bigl[C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)\bigr]
 \;\xrightarrow{\;\varepsilon\to 0\;}\;u(t,x)-f(x),
\]
where $u(t,x)=\E[f(x+X_{|Y_t|})]$ is the Brownian-time semigroup
applied to $f$. The limit decomposes as
\[
 u(t,x)-f(x)
 \;=\;\underbrace{\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\tfrac12\!\E_Y\!\int_0^t\!\phi_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{int}}(|Y_s|)\,ds}_{\text{interior bi-Laplacian shadow}}
   \;+\;\underbrace{\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\tfrac12\!\E_Y\!\int_0^t\!b_\varepsilon(|Y_s|)\,ds}_{\text{boundary-layer source}};
\]
the boundary-layer piece converges in expectation to
$\int_0^t\Delta f(x)/(2\sqrt{2\pi s})\,ds$ via the EF Brownian-time
PDE consistency~\cite[Thm.\ 6.4]{Fontes-EnergyFirst}; we identify
this limit only at the level of expectations, not as a full random
$L^{2}(\Omega_Y)$ limit of the boundary-layer functional.
\item (Clock-fluctuation blocks) For $n\ge 1$,
$\Pir_{0,n}=\Pir_n^Y F_\varepsilon$ is a centred element of
$\Hilb_n^Y$, and in particular
\[
 \Pir_{0,1}\,C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)
 \;=\;I_1^Y\!\bigl(\E_Y[D^Y_\cdot F_\varepsilon(Y;t)]\bigr)
\]
by the Stroock--Clark--Ocone formula, where
$D^Y_u|Y_s|=\sgn(Y_s)\mathbf 1_{u\le s}$ on the standard
Bouleau--Hirsch domain.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

title: C: first-scenery-chaos bidegree slices
extraction: mechanical declaration index, not a proof certificate
statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[C: first-scenery-chaos bidegree slices]
\label{thm:first-chaos}
For every $f\in\mathscr S(\R)$, $t\ge 0$, $\varepsilon>0$, $n\ge 0$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Block formula)
\[
 \Pir_{1,n}\,C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)
 \;=\;I_1^X\!\bigl(\Pir_n^Y K_\varepsilon(\cdot\mid Y)\bigr).
\]
\item (Clock-averaged block, $n=0$)
\[
 \Pir_{1,0}\,C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)
 \;=\;I_1^X\!\bigl(\E_Y K_\varepsilon(\cdot\mid Y)\bigr).
\]
This sector has zero full expectation
($\E[\Pir_{1,0}C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}]=\E[I_1^X(\E_Y K_\varepsilon)]=0$)
but is generally non-zero as an element of $\Hilb_1^X$.
\item (FCDC closure inheritance, at the level of kernels) The FCDC
convergence~\cite[Thm.\ 5.3]{Fontes-FCDC} of the conditional
Malliavin kernel descends block-by-block to the $Y$-chaos
projections: as $\varepsilon\to 0$,
\[
 \Pir_n^Y K_\varepsilon(\cdot\mid Y)
 \;\longrightarrow\;\Pir_n^Y K^{\mathrm{lim}}(\cdot\mid Y)
\quad\text{in }L^{2}(\Omega_Y;H^{-1}(\R)),
\]
where $K^{\mathrm{lim}}=K^{\mathrm{int}}+L_t^0(Y)f'(x)\delta_0$ is
the FCDC limit kernel. In particular, the clock-averaged kernels
satisfy $\E_Y K_\varepsilon\to\E_Y K^{\mathrm{lim}}$ in $H^{-1}(\R)$.
The corresponding first-chaos dual element
$\Pir_{1,n}C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}=I_1^X(\Pir_n^Y K_\varepsilon)$ is
therefore convergent in the first-chaos dual topology of FCDC, i.e.\
the topology induced on $\Hilb_1^X$-valued objects with conditional
kernel in $L^{2}(\Omega_Y;H^{-1}(\R))$; we do \emph{not} assert that
the limit lies in $L^{2}(\Omega)$ as an ordinary random variable.
Under the additional EF non-degeneracy condition
$(P_\eta f')(x)\not\equiv 0$ on $(0,\infty)$, the $(1,\bullet)$
sector closed here is precisely the one whose classical
$L^{2}(\Omega)$ variance diverges (\eqref{eq:obstr}), so the
dual-topology closure is forced by the failure of classical
$L^{2}(\Omega)$ convergence; we do not claim $H^{-1}(\R)$ is the
optimal Sobolev threshold.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

extraction: mechanical declaration index, not a proof certificate
statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Channel enumeration]\label{prop:channels}
For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and $r\ge 0$,
\begin{align*}
 \Pir_2^X\!\bigl[f''(x+U_r)V_r^2\bigr]
 &=\;\Channel{0,0}+\Channel{2,V}+\Channel{2,\mathrm{c}}+\Channel{4},\\
 \Pir_2^X\!\bigl[f'(x+U_r)W_r\bigr]
 &=\;\Channel{1}+\Channel{3},
\end{align*}
where, writing $h^{(k)}_{m,r}$ for $h^{(k)}_{m,r,\varepsilon}$ to
declutter:
\begin{align*}
 \Channel{0,0}\;\;&\coloneqq\;\E_X[f''(x+U_r)]\cdot I_2^X(\rho_\varepsilon(r-\cdot)^{\otimes 2})
   &&\text{(scalar $\cdot$ $:V_r^2:$),}\\
 \Channel{2,V}&\coloneqq\;\sigma_V^2\cdot I_2^X(h^{(2)}_{2,r})
   &&\text{($\sigma_V^2$ $\cdot$ chaos-2 of $f''$),}\\
 \Channel{2,\mathrm{c}}&\coloneqq\;4\cdot I_2^X\bigl(h^{(2)}_{2,r}\otimes_1\rho_\varepsilon(r-\cdot)^{\otimes 2}\bigr)
   &&\text{(1-contraction, chaos-2 of $f''$ vs.\ $:V_r^2:$),}\\
 \Channel{4}&\coloneqq\;12\cdot I_2^X\bigl(h^{(2)}_{4,r}\otimes_2\rho_\varepsilon(r-\cdot)^{\otimes 2}\bigr)
   &&\text{(2-contraction, chaos-4 of $f''$ vs.\ $:V_r^2:$),}\\
 \Channel{1}&\coloneqq\;I_2^X\bigl(h^{(1)}_{1,r}\,\widetilde\otimes\,\rho_\varepsilon'(r-\cdot)\bigr)
   &&\text{(no-contraction $I_1\cdot I_1$, chaos-1 of $f'$ vs.\ $W_r$),}\\
 \Channel{3}&\coloneqq\;3\cdot I_2^X\bigl(h^{(1)}_{3,r}\otimes_1\rho_\varepsilon'(r-\cdot)\bigr)
   &&\text{(1-contraction, chaos-3 of $f'$ vs.\ $W_r$).}
\end{align*}
There are no further chaos-2 contributions: for $q\in\{0,2\}$
(arising from $V_r^2$), $p+q-2j=2$ and $j\le\min(p,q)$ together
force $p\in\{0,2,4\}$ with $p$ even; for $q=1$ (arising from $W_r$),
$p+1-2j=2$ forces $p$ odd with $p\le q+2=3$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{definition}[Observable It\^o identity]\label{def:obs-ito-identity}
Let $\mathcal T\subseteq C(\R)$ be a class of test functions and
$X=(X_t)_{t\ge 0}$ an $\R$-valued process with
$\E|f(X_t)|<\infty$ for every $f\in\mathcal T$ and $t\ge 0$. We
say that $X$ admits an \emph{observable It\^o identity} on
$\mathcal T$ if, for each $f\in\mathcal T$, the map
$t\mapsto\E[f(X_t)]$ is locally absolutely continuous on
$(0,\infty)$ and there exist a family of linear operators
$\mathcal G_t$ on $\mathcal T$ and a family of linear functionals
$\mathcal B_t$ on $\mathcal T$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:obs-ito-identity}
  \frac{d}{dt}\,\E[f(X_t)]
   \;=\;\E\bigl[(\mathcal G_t f)(X_t)\bigr]
   \;+\;\mathcal B_t f
\end{equation}
in the sense of distributions in $t$, or pointwise wherever the
left-hand-side derivative exists.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Energy datum]\label{def:energy-datum}
An \emph{energy datum} is a triple $(\Hilb,\Energy, D)$ where
$\Hilb\subseteq L^2(\Omega)$ is a closed subspace,
$\Energy$ is a separable Hilbert space, and
\[
  D\colon \Dom(D)\subseteq\Hilb \longrightarrow \Energy
\]
is a closed, densely defined linear operator. The
\emph{divergence} is the Hilbert-space adjoint
$\delta\coloneqq D^{*}\colon\Dom(\delta)\subseteq\Energy\to\Hilb$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Mollified scenery and mollified core]
\label{def:mollified}
Fix a non-negative even mollifier $\rho\in C_c^\infty(\R)$ with
$\int\rho=1$ and write $\rho_\varepsilon(z)=\varepsilon^{-1}\rho(z/\varepsilon)$.
The $\varepsilon$-mollified scenery is
\[
  X^{\varepsilon}_y \;\coloneqq\; (\rho_\varepsilon*X)(y)
  \;=\;\int_{\R}\rho_\varepsilon(y-z)\,X_z\,dz,
  \qquad y\in\R,
\]
which is $\Prob$-a.s.\ $C^{\infty}$ in $y$ on every compact, with
$X^{\varepsilon}_y\to X_y$ locally uniformly in $y$ a.s.\ as
$\varepsilon\to 0$ by Brownian H\"older continuity. The
$\varepsilon$-mollified occupation functional is
\[
  F_{T,\varepsilon}(\varphi)
  \;\coloneqq\;\int_0^T\varphi\bigl(X^{\varepsilon}_{Y_s}\bigr)\,ds,
\]
and the associated mollified core is
\[
  \mathcal C_{\mathrm{occ}}^{\,\varepsilon}
  \;\coloneqq\;\mathrm{span}\bigl\{\,F_{T,\varepsilon}(\varphi)-
      \E F_{T,\varepsilon}(\varphi):T>0,\ \varphi\in\mathscr S_\IBM\,\bigr\}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Mollified-to-unmollified IBM occupation convergence in the scenery direction]
\label{thm:ibm-occ}
Let $T>0$ and $\varphi\in\mathscr S_\IBM=C_c^\infty(\R)$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $\varepsilon>0$,
  $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{occ}}^{\,\varepsilon}\subseteq\mathcal C_\IBM$,
  and the occupation-core intrinsic derivative
  $D_\IBM^{\,\mathrm{occ},\,\varepsilon}$ is the restriction of the
  minimal observable derivative $D_\IBM$ of \cref{def:ibm-datum} to
  $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{occ}}^{\,\varepsilon}$, with explicit kernels
  \eqref{eq:DX-moll}--\eqref{eq:DY-moll}.
\item On the lifted source-divergence domain, the adjoint
  $\delta_\IBM^{\,\mathrm{occ},\,\varepsilon}$ admits the projected
  formula \eqref{eq:occ-delta}.
\item As $\varepsilon\to 0$,
  $F_{T,\varepsilon}(\varphi)\to F_T(\varphi)$ in $L^{2}(\Omega)$, with
  rate $O(\varepsilon^{1/2})$.
\item As $\varepsilon\to 0$,
  $D_X F_{T,\varepsilon}(\varphi)\to D_X F_T(\varphi)$ in
  $L^{2}(\Omega;L^{2}(\R))$, also at rate $O(\varepsilon^{1/2})$, with
  limit
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:DX-limit}
    D_X F_T(\varphi)(\xi)
    \;=\;\int_{\R}\varphi'(X_x)\,\sigma_x(\xi)\,L_T^{\,x}(Y)\,dx
    \;=\;\int_0^T\varphi'(X_{Y_s})\,\sigma_{Y_s}(\xi)\,ds.
  \end{equation}
\item For every $\varepsilon>0$, $D_Y F_{T,\varepsilon}(\varphi)$ is a
  classical element of $L^{2}(\R_{+})$ given by \eqref{eq:DY-moll}. The

\label{thm:bt-correction}
Let $X$ be standard two-sided Brownian scenery with $\Var(X_s)=s$ and
$Y$ an independent standard Brownian clock. For $f\in C_c^{\infty}(\R)$

\end{theorem}

statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Energy-first It\^o formula for mollified IBM]
\label{thm:energy-first-ito-moll}
Let $X$ be standard two-sided Brownian scenery with $\Var(X_s)=|s|$,
$Y$ an independent standard Brownian clock, $\rho$ an even
non-negative compactly supported mollifier, $X^\varepsilon=
\rho_\varepsilon*X$, and
\[
  \IBM_t^{\,\varepsilon}\;\coloneqq\;x+X^\varepsilon_{|Y_t|},
  \qquad t\ge 0,\;x\in\R.
\]
For $f\in\mathscr S(\R)$, set $g_\varepsilon(r)\coloneqq
f(x+X^\varepsilon_r)$, $r\in\R$, which is $\Prob_X$-a.s.\ $C^\infty$
in $r$. Then for every $\varepsilon>0$ and $t\ge 0$:

\smallskip
\noindent\textbf{(i) Mollified pathwise It\^o--Tanaka identity.}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:efi-ito}
  f(\IBM_t^{\,\varepsilon})-f(\IBM_0^{\,\varepsilon})
  \;=\;\delta_Y\bigl(B_{f,\varepsilon}(t)\bigr)
   \;+\;C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t),
\end{equation}
with clock-divergence integrand
\begin{equation}\label{eq:efi-B}
  B_{f,\varepsilon}(t)(s)
   \;=\;g_\varepsilon'(|Y_s|)\,\mathrm{sgn}(Y_s)\,
        \mathbf 1_{[0,t]}(s),
\end{equation}
and mollified pathwise correction
\begin{equation}\label{eq:efi-C}
  C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)
   \;=\;g_\varepsilon'(0)\,L_t^{0}(Y)
   \;+\;\tfrac12\!\int_0^t g_\varepsilon''(|Y_s|)\,ds,
\end{equation}
where $L_t^{0}(Y)$ is the Brownian local time of $Y$ at $0$ and the
clock derivatives are explicit:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:efi-gpp}
  g_\varepsilon'(r)
   \;=\;f'(x+X^\varepsilon_r)\,\partial_rX^\varepsilon_r,\qquad
  g_\varepsilon''(r)
   \;=\;f''(x+X^\varepsilon_r)\,(\partial_rX^\varepsilon_r)^{2}
   \;+\;f'(x+X^\varepsilon_r)\,\partial_r^{2}X^\varepsilon_r.
\end{equation}

\smallskip
\noindent\textbf{(ii) Operator-divergence reading of the martingale
term.} The term $\delta_Y(B_{f,\varepsilon}(t))$ in \eqref{eq:efi-ito}
is the source clock Skorohod divergence of the integrand
\eqref{eq:efi-B}; it coincides pathwise with the conditional It\^o
integral $\int_0^t g_\varepsilon'(|Y_s|)\,\mathrm{sgn}(Y_s)\,dY_s$, is
a continuous $L^{2}$-martingale in $Y$ (conditional on $X$), and
satisfies $\E[\delta_Y(B_{f,\varepsilon}(t))]=0$. In the language of
the conditional operator-It\^o transfer principle
(\cref{thm:transfer}), \eqref{eq:efi-ito} is the mollified instance
of the schematic pathwise target \eqref{eq:pathwise-target}, with the
clock-source divergence carrying the martingale part.

\smallskip
\noindent\textbf{(iii) Fourth-order expectation-level consistency.}
With $u(t,x)=\E[f(x+X_{|Y_t|})]$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:efi-fourth}
  \lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\E\bigl[C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)\bigr]
   \;=\;\int_0^t\!\Bigl[\,\tfrac{1}{8}\,\partial_x^{4}u(s,x)
        \;+\;\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2\pi s}}\,\partial_x^{2}f(x)\,\Bigr]\,ds
   \;=\;u(t,x)-f(x).
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\[
 \Energy_{\IBM,1}^{+}\;\coloneqq\;L^{2}(\Omega_Y;H^{1}(\R,dw)),
 \qquad
 \Energy_{\IBM,1}^{-}\;\coloneqq\;L^{2}(\Omega_Y;H^{-1}(\R,dw)),
\]
with the fibrewise duality pairing
$\langle K(\cdot\mid Y),\Phi(\cdot\mid Y)\rangle_{H^{-1},H^{1}}$
extending the $L^{2}(\R)$ inner product on each fibre. A
\emph{generalized $Y$-conditioned first-chaos functional} is an
object specified by a kernel
$K\in\Energy_{\IBM,1}^{-}=L^{2}(\Omega_Y;H^{-1}(\R))$; it acts on
$Y$-random test integrands $\Phi\in\Energy_{\IBM,1}^{+}=L^{2}(\Omega_Y;H^{1}(\R))$
by the \emph{first-chaos pairing}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:first-chaos-pairing}
 \bigl\langle K,\Phi\bigr\rangle_{1,*}
 \;\coloneqq\;\E_{Y}\!\bigl[\langle K(\cdot\mid Y),\Phi(\cdot\mid Y)\rangle_{H^{-1},H^{1}}\bigr],
\end{equation}
finite by Cauchy--Schwarz in $L^{2}(\Omega_Y)$. A deterministic test
$\phi\in H^{1}(\R)$ is the special case $\Phi(Y,w)=\phi(w)$. When
$K(\cdot\mid Y)\in L^{2}(\R)$ a.s., the pairing reduces to the
fibrewise $L^{2}(\R)$-pairing and the functional is realised by the
ordinary first-chaos random variable
$I_1^X(K(\cdot\mid Y))\in L^{2}(\Omega)$; when $K(\cdot\mid Y)$ is
only in $H^{-1}(\R)$, no such $L^{2}(\Omega_X)$ random variable
exists, and the functional is specified by~\eqref{eq:first-chaos-pairing}
alone, on $Y$-random test kernels $\Phi$ identified fibrewise with
first-chaos test variables $I_1^X(\Phi(\cdot\mid Y))$.
\end{definition}

evaluation of the scenery at the clock $X_{|Y_t|}$, which lies

scenario the natural home for the unmollified pathwise correction

extraction: mechanical declaration index, not a proof certificate
statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Pure-clock sector and expectation limit]
\label{thm:pure-clock}
For every $f\in\mathscr S(\R)$, $t\ge 0$, $\varepsilon>0$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Scalar identity)
\[
 \Pir_0^X\,C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)
 \;=\;F_\varepsilon(Y;t)
 \;\coloneqq\;\tfrac12\!\int_0^t\!\psi_\varepsilon(|Y_s|)\,ds,
\]
with $\psi_\varepsilon=\phi_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{int}}+b_\varepsilon$
as in \eqref{eq:phi-int-def}.
\item (Bidegree slices) For every $n\ge 0$,
$\Pir_{0,n}\,C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)=\Pir_n^Y F_\varepsilon(Y;t)$.
\item (Expectation limit, referring to \cref{thm:moll-consistency})
\[
 \Pir_{0,0}\,C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)
 \;=\;\E\!\bigl[C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)\bigr]
 \;\xrightarrow{\;\varepsilon\to 0\;}\;u(t,x)-f(x).
\]
The limit decomposes as
\[
 u(t,x)-f(x)
 \;=\;\underbrace{\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\tfrac12\E_Y\!\int_0^t\phi_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{int}}(|Y_s|)\,ds}_{\text{interior bi-Laplacian shadow}}
   \;+\;\underbrace{\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\tfrac12\E_Y\!\int_0^t b_\varepsilon(|Y_s|)\,ds}_{\text{boundary-layer source}};
\]
the boundary-layer piece converges in expectation to
$\int_0^t\partial_x^{2}f(x)/(2\sqrt{2\pi s})\,ds$. We identify this
limit only at the level of expectations; see \cref{flag:bdy-layer}.
\item (Clock-fluctuation blocks) For $n\ge 1$,
$\Pir_{0,n}=\Pir_n^Y F_\varepsilon$ is centred in $\Hilb_n^Y$. In
particular, by Stroock--Clark--Ocone~\cite{Nualart},
\[
 \Pir_{0,1}\,C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)
 \;=\;I_1^Y\!\bigl(\E_Y[D^Y_\cdot F_\varepsilon(Y;t)]\bigr),
\]
with $D^Y_u|Y_s|=\sgn(Y_s)\mathbf 1_{u\le s}$ on the standard
Bouleau--Hirsch domain.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[First-scenery-chaos bidegree slices]
\label{thm:first-chaos}
For every $f\in\mathscr S(\R)$, $t\ge 0$, $\varepsilon>0$, $n\ge 0$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Block formula)
$\Pir_{1,n}\,C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)=I_1^X(\Pir_n^Y K_\varepsilon(\cdot\mid Y))$.
\item (Clock-averaged block, $n=0$)
$\Pir_{1,0}\,C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}(f;t)=I_1^X(\E_Y K_\varepsilon(\cdot\mid Y))$.
This sector has zero full expectation (every $\Hilb_1^X$ element is
centred in $X$) but is generally non-zero as an element of $\Hilb_1^X$.
\item (Dual closure inheritance) The dual closure of
\cref{cor:combined} descends block-by-block: as $\varepsilon\to 0$,
$\Pir_n^Y K_\varepsilon\to\Pir_n^Y K^{\mathrm{lim}}$ in
$L^{2}(\Omega_Y;H^{-1}(\R))$, with $K^{\mathrm{lim}}=K^{\mathrm{int}}+L_t^{0}(Y)f'(x)\delta_0$.
In particular $\E_Y K_\varepsilon\to\E_Y K^{\mathrm{lim}}$ in
$H^{-1}(\R)$. The convergence is at the level of conditional
Malliavin kernels; the corresponding first-chaos objects
$\Pir_{1,n}C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}$ are ordinary
$L^{2}(\Omega)$-valued random variables at every fixed
$\varepsilon>0$, but their limit is the generalized
$Y$-conditioned first-chaos functional of
\cref{def:first-chaos-block} specified by the kernel
$\Pir_n^Y K^{\mathrm{lim}}\in L^{2}(\Omega_Y;H^{-1}(\R))$ via the
duality pairing, not an ordinary $L^{2}(\Omega)$-valued random
variable.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[Scalar Wick subtraction does not remove the first-chaos obstruction]
\label{prop:wick-insufficient}
Under the hypotheses of \cref{thm:var-divergence}, the contraction
subtraction~\eqref{eq:wick-sq} does not modify the
$\partial_r^{2}X^\varepsilon$ content of $g_\varepsilon''$, so the
first-scenery-chaos singularity in $\Pir_1^X C_{\IBM,\varepsilon}$
carried by $\partial_r^{2}X^\varepsilon$ (identified
in~\cref{thm:var-divergence}) is not removed. In addition, the
subtraction introduces a counterterm whose first-chaos contribution
is large, so the Stein cancellation that isolates the $T_3$
singularity is not preserved. Scalar Wick-square subtraction
therefore does not remove the first-chaos obstruction and cannot by
itself provide the stabilising renormalisation of the full
correction.
\end{proposition}

statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Noise]\label{def:noise}
A \emph{noise} on $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\Prob)$ is a system
$\mathcal N=\bigl((\mathcal F_{s,t})_{s\le t},(T_h)_{h\in\R}\bigr)$
of sub-$\sigma$-fields and a measurable measure-preserving group
action, satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item[$(\mathrm i)$] \emph{Independent factorization.} For every
$r\le s\le t$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:noise-factor}
  \mathcal F_{r,t}\;=\;\mathcal F_{r,s}\vee\mathcal F_{s,t},
  \qquad \mathcal F_{r,s}\perp\!\!\!\perp\mathcal F_{s,t}.
\end{equation}
\item[$(\mathrm{ii})$] \emph{Stationarity.} Each
$T_h\colon\Omega\to\Omega$ is measure preserving,
$T_{h_1+h_2}=T_{h_1}\circ T_{h_2}$, and
$T_h(\mathcal F_{s,t})=\mathcal F_{s+h,\,t+h}$.
\item[$(\mathrm{iii})$] \emph{Continuity.} The standard continuity
conditions on $(\mathcal F_{s,t})$ in $(s,t)$ hold (right-continuity
at right endpoints; left-continuity at left endpoints).
\end{itemize}
We refer to~\cite{Tsirelson2004}, \S 2, for the full
Tsirelson--Vershik axioms; the form above is sufficient for the
present paper.
\end{definition}

valued in $(H_{s,t})$, is a family

title: Coalescing Brownian flow: formal diagonal defect
extraction: mechanical declaration index, not a proof certificate
statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Coalescing Brownian flow: formal diagonal defect]\label{prop:defect-coalescing}
Let $\Phi$ be Arratia's coalescing Brownian flow on $\R$, in which
distinct points evolve as independent Brownian motions until they
meet and coalesce, and as a single Brownian motion thereafter. For
$f,g\in C_c^{\infty}(\R)$:
\begin{itemize}
\item[$(\mathrm a)$] \emph{Off-diagonal vanishing.} On
$\{(x,y)\in\R^{2}:x\neq y\}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:defect-coalescing-offdiag}
  \mathfrak D^{(2)}(f,g)(x,y)\;=\;0.
\end{equation}
\item[$(\mathrm b)$] \emph{Diagonal density.} On the diagonal
$\{x=y\}$, with the identification
$(f\otimes g)(x,x)=(fg)(x)$ inherited from the coalescence rule,
the two-point generator acts as
$L^{(2)}(f\otimes g)(x,x)=L^{(1)}(fg)(x)=\tfrac{1}{2}(fg)''(x)$, so
the pointwise diagonal value of the product defect is the one-point
carr\'e-du-champ of the heat semigroup,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:defect-coalescing-diag}
  \mathfrak D^{(2)}(f,g)(x,x)
  \;=\;f'(x)g'(x)
  \;=\;2\,\Gamma^{(1)}(f,g)(x).
\end{equation}
\end{itemize}
In particular $\mathfrak D^{(2)}(f,g)$ is a product-defect
distribution supported on the diagonal $\{x=y\}$, with formal density
$f'(x)g'(x)$ in the variable $x$. The normalization of
$\mathfrak D^{(2)}(f,g)$ as a distribution on $\R^{2}$ --- against the
diagonal Lebesgue measure, against the local-time measure of
$Y_t-X_t$ at $0$, or against any other choice --- is inherited from
the generator and domain convention adopted for the coalescing flow.
\end{proposition}

title: Brownian sticky flow: conditional defect
extraction: mechanical declaration index, not a proof certificate
statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Brownian sticky flow: conditional defect]\label{prop:defect-sticky}
Let $\Phi_{\theta}$ be the Brownian sticky flow of
\cite{LeJanRaimond2004} with sticky parameter $\theta$. Suppose
the two-point generator $L^{(2)}_{\theta}$ acts on a suitable test
class as $\tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_x^2+\partial_y^2)$ off the diagonal
$\{x=y\}$, subject to the Wentzell-type sticky boundary condition
prescribed by \cite{LeJanRaimond2004}. Then the product defect of
\cref{def:two-point-defect} vanishes off the diagonal,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:defect-sticky-offdiag}
  \mathfrak D^{(2)}_{\theta}(f,g)(x,y)\;=\;0\qquad\text{for }x\neq y,
\end{equation}
and is concentrated as a diagonal-supported product-defect
distribution on $\{x=y\}$. The diagonal coefficient is governed by
the sticky boundary condition; it vanishes at the independent-flow
endpoint of the parametrization (recovering
\cref{prop:defect-indep}), and at the coalescing endpoint of the
parametrization the diagonal formal density is $f'(x)g'(x)$ in the
sense of \cref{prop:defect-coalescing}, with normalization
determined by the chosen generator/domain convention.
\end{proposition}

The \emph{$N$-point product defect} of the flow $\Phi$ on
$f_1,\ldots,f_N\in\mathcal T^{(1)}$ is the object
\begin{equation}\label{eq:N-point-defect}
  \mathfrak D^{(N)}(f_1,\ldots,f_N)
  \;:=\;
  L^{(N)}(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_N)
  \;-\;\sum_{i=1}^{N}(L^{(1)}f_i)\otimes\prod_{j\neq i}f_j,
\end{equation}
initially defined on the common domain of the $N$-point generator
$L^{(N)}$ and of the one-point generator $L^{(1)}$ acting in each
factor, and interpreted according to the $N$-point generator/domain
convention --- as a function, an energy measure, or a distribution
on $\R^{N}$ (or on its symmetric quotient as appropriate). In
particular the diagonal-supported product defects of the coalescing
and sticky flows in
\cref{prop:defect-coalescing,prop:defect-sticky} are read as
distributions on $\R^{2}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Generator-level interaction hierarchy]\label{def:N-point-cdc}
For a finite index set $S$ with $|S|\ge 2$ and one-point test
functions $(f_i)_{i\in S}\subset\mathcal T^{(1)}$, define the
\emph{generator-level interaction defect} $\Gamma_S$ on $S$
recursively by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gamma-N-cumulant}
  \Gamma_S(f_S)
  \;:=\;
  M_S(f_S)
  \;-\;
  \!\!\sum_{\substack{B\subsetneq S\\ |B|\ge 2}}\!\!
  \Gamma_B(f_B)\prod_{j\in S\setminus B}f_j,
\end{equation}
read in the appropriate distribution / energy-measure / function
space on $\R^{|S|}$ inherited from the $|S|$-point generator/domain
convention. The base case $|S|=2$ gives
$\Gamma_{\{i,j\}}(f_if_j)=M_{\{i,j\}}(f_if_j)=\Gamma^{(2)}(f_i,f_j)$,
the bilinear two-point carr\'e-du-champ.
Equivalently, on every $S$ the recursion is the subset inversion of
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gamma-N-inversion}
  M_S(f_S)
  \;=\;
  \!\!\sum_{\substack{B\subseteq S\\ |B|\ge 2}}\!\!
  \Gamma_B(f_B)\prod_{j\in S\setminus B}f_j.
\end{equation}
We refer to $\{\Gamma_S\}_{|S|\ge 2}$ as the \emph{generator-level
interaction hierarchy} (or, equivalently, the
\emph{infinitesimal product-defect hierarchy}); the members
$\Gamma_S$ for $|S|\ge 3$ are the \emph{higher
$\Gamma$-interaction defects} of the flow. The bilinear $|S|=2$
member is the proper carr\'e-du-champ; the higher members are
$|S|$-linear interaction defects, not bilinear carr\'es-du-champ.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[$\Proj^Y_2 \Loc_T^x(Y)$]
\label{lem:proj2-LT}
For $x \in \R$ and $T > 0$,
\begin{equation}
  \Proj^Y_2 \Loc_T^x(Y)
   \;=\; \psi_T(x)\,\bigl(Y_T^2 - T\bigr)
        \,-\, 2 \int_0^T \psi_s(x)\,Y_s\,dY_s,
   \label{eq:proj2-LT}
\end{equation}
equivalently $I_2^Y\bigl(K_T(\cdot, \cdot; x)\bigr)$ as a double
Wiener--It\^o integral with symmetric kernel
$K_T(s_1, s_2; x) = \psi_T(x) - \psi_{\max(s_1, s_2)}(x)$. The kernel
is in $L^2([0, T]^2)$ for each $x$, including $x = 0$. In any case,
changing the value at the singleton $\{x = 0\}$ does not affect the
spatial Bochner integral of \eqref{eq:source-projection}. This is the
$n = 2$ specialisation of the Nualart--Vives chaos expansion of
Brownian local time \cite{NualartVives}, with the Brownian-heat-kernel
normalisation $\psi_t(x) = (2 \pi t)^{-1/2} e^{-x^2/(2t)}$ used here.
\end{lemma}

extraction: mechanical declaration index, not a proof certificate
statement_tex:
\begin{mainthm}[Unified Clark--Ocone representation]\label{thmA}
Let $X$ have energy space~$\HX$, centered isometric stochastic integral $\delta_X$, predictable projection $\Pi_X$, and $D_X = \delta_X^*$. Assume $X$ has the predictable representation property. Then for every ${\FX}_T$-measurable $F \in L^2(\Omega)$:
\[
F \;=\; \E[F] + \delta_X(\Pi_X D_X F).
\]
Without PRP, $\delta_X(\Pi_X D_X F) = \mathrm{proj}_{\mathcal{S}_X}(F - \E[F])$, the orthogonal projection onto the stable subspace $\mathcal{S}_X = \overline{\{\delta_X(u) : u \textup{ predictable}\}}^{L^2}$.
\end{mainthm}

title: Cylindrical reduction implies Leibniz
extraction: mechanical declaration index, not a proof certificate
statement_tex:
\begin{mainthm}[Cylindrical reduction implies Leibniz]\label{thmB}
Let $(\delta_X, \HX)$ admit a cylindrical structure: a dense class $\mathcal{C} = \{f(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n) : f \in C_b^\infty\}$ of functionals with representers $\kappa_i \in L^2(\Omega;\HX)$ satisfying the integration-by-parts formula
\[
\E[F\cdot\delta_X(u)] = \sum_{i=1}^n \E[\partial_if(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n)\cdot\langle\kappa_i,u\rangle_{\HX}].
\]
Then $D_X$ satisfies the Leibniz rule $D_X(FG) = F\,D_X G + G\,D_X F$ on $\mathbb{D}^{1,4}(\Omega) := \overline{\mathcal{C}}^{\|\cdot\|_{1,4}}$, the chain rule $D_X(\varphi(F)) = \varphi'(F)\,D_X F$ for $\varphi \in C_b^\infty$, and the product rule $\delta_X(Fu) = F\,\delta_X(u) - \langle D_X F, u \rangle_{\HX}$ for $F \in \dom(D_X)\cap L^\infty$ with $\|D_XF\|_{\HX}\|u\|_{\HX} \in L^2(\Omega)$.
\end{mainthm}

title: Operator It\^o formula (abstract scheme)
extraction: mechanical declaration index, not a proof certificate
statement_tex:
\begin{mainthm}[Operator It\^o formula (abstract scheme)]\label{thmC}
Let $(D,\delta,\Pi)$ satisfy the chain rule with $\Pi$ an orthogonal projection, and assume the factorization $(\Id-\E)G = \delta(\Pi DG)$ holds for $G = \varphi(Y_t)$. Let $Y$ be a $(D,\delta,\Pi)$-It\^o process: $Y_t = Y_0 + \int_0^t a_s\,ds + \delta(\Pi DY \cdot \mathbf{1}_{[0,t]})$ with $t \mapsto \Pi DY_t$ H\"older continuous in $L^2(\Omega;\mathcal{H})$. Assume the Skorokhod isometry with remainder holds on short intervals, and that a stochastic Fubini interchange is valid for the divergence integrands (see Theorem~\ref{thm:ito} for precise conditions). Then for $\varphi \in C_b^3(\R)$:
\[
\varphi(Y_t) = \varphi(Y_0) + \int_0^t\varphi'(Y_s)\,a_s\,ds + \delta(\varphi'(Y)\,\Pi DY\cdot\mathbf{1}_{[0,t]}) + \frac{1}{2}\int_0^t\varphi''(Y_s)\,\|\Pi DY_s\|^2_{\mathcal{H}}\,ds
\]
in $L^2(\Omega)$, with intrinsic bracket $\langle Y\rangle_t^{(D,\Pi)} := \int_0^t\|\Pi DY_s\|^2_{\mathcal{H}}\,ds$. These conditions are verified for Gaussian Volterra processes~\cite{Decreusefond1999} and for standard It\^o martingales.
\end{mainthm}

\begin{mainthm}[Leibniz for stochastic volatility]\label{thmD}
Let $M_t = \int_0^t\sigma_s\,dW_s$ where $W$ is standard Brownian motion and $\sigma$ is progressively measurable with $\sigma_t > 0$ a.s., $\E[\int_0^T\sigma_t^2\,dt] < \infty$, and $\sigma_t \in \mathbb{D}^{1,2}$ for a.e.~$t$ with $\E[\int_0^T\|D^W\sigma_t\|^2_{L^2[0,T]}\,dt] < \infty$. On the extended energy space $\HM^{\mathrm{ext}} := L^2([0,T]\times\Omega,\,\sigma_t^2\,dt\otimes dP)$, the operator derivative $(D_MF)_t = D_t^WF/\sigma_t$ satisfies the Leibniz rule:
\[
D_M(FG) = F\,D_MG + G\,D_MF \qquad\text{for } F,G \in \mathbb{D}^{1,4}(\Omega).
\]
The cylindrical reduction uses random representers $\kappa_i(t) = D_t^W(M_{t_i})/\sigma_t$, which reduce to the deterministic $\mathbf{1}_{[0,t_i]}(t)$ when $\sigma$ is deterministic.
\end{mainthm}

\begin{mainthm}[Gubinelli derivative as predictable projection]\label{thmF}
Let $\BH$ be fractional Brownian motion with $H \in (0,1)$, $H \neq 1/2$, and $F \in L^2(\Omega,{\FBH}_T)$ with $D_{\BH}F \in L^2(\Omega;\HH)$. Let $Y_t := \E[F\mid{\FBH}_t]$. Then
\[
Y_t - Y_s = \langle(\Pi_{\BH}D_{\BH}F)_s,\, k_t - k_s\rangle_{\HH} + R_{s,t}, \qquad \E[R_{s,t}^2] = O(|t-s|^{\min(4H,\,2H+1)}),
\]
where $k_t$ is the evaluation representer in the Cameron--Martin space $\HH$. The object $(\Pi_{\BH}D_{\BH}F)_s$ is the Gubinelli derivative in $L^2$. For $H < 1/2$, the remainder exponent is $4H$; for $H > 1/2$, it is $2H + 1 > 2$, giving even faster decay.
\end{mainthm}

\begin{lemma}[Malliavin sensitivity as an It\^o integral]\label{lem:mall_ito}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:sv}, for a.e.\ $t \in [0,T]$ and each $t_j \in [0,T]$ with $t \le t_j$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item The Malliavin derivative of $M_{t_j}$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:mall_ito}
D_t^W(M_{t_j}) = \sigma_t + \int_t^{t_j} D_t^W(\sigma_s)\,dW_s.
\end{equation}
\item The process $s \mapsto D_t^W(\sigma_s)\,\mathbf{1}_{[t,t_j]}(s)$ is $\mathcal{F}_s$-adapted and square-integrable:
\[
\E\!\left[\int_t^{t_j} |D_t^W(\sigma_s)|^2\,ds\right] < \infty.
\]
\item The integral $\int_t^{t_j} D_t^W(\sigma_s)\,dW_s$ is a genuine It\^o integral, hence centered:
\[
\E\!\left[\int_t^{t_j} D_t^W(\sigma_s)\,dW_s\right] = 0.
\]
\item The It\^o isometry applies:
\[
\E\!\left[\left(\int_t^{t_j} D_t^W(\sigma_s)\,dW_s\right)^{\!2}\right] = \E\!\left[\int_t^{t_j} |D_t^W(\sigma_s)|^2\,ds\right].
\]
\end{enumerate}
For $t > t_j$: $D_t^W(M_{t_j}) = 0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Spatial regularity]\label{thm:spatial_reg}
Let $\alpha = 2H_2$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\alph*)}]
\item \emph{Deterministic smoothing.}  For $f \in L^2(\R)$
and $t > 0$, $S_t f \in H^s(\R)$ for every
$0 \leq s \leq 2H_1$, with
$\norm{S_t f}_{H^s} \leq C(s,t,H_1,H_2)\,\norm{f}_{L^2}$.
\item \emph{Trace-class noise.}  If $Q$ is trace-class,
the stochastic convolution
$\int_0^t \Phi_{t-r}\, dB_r$ belongs to $H^s(\R)$ provided
\begin{equation}\label{eq:spatial_reg_trace}
\int_0^t \norm{(I-\Delta)^{s/2} \Phi_r Q^{1/2}}_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\,
dr < \infty.
\end{equation}
Without additional smoothing of $Q$, the operator-norm
estimate
$\norm{(I-\Delta)^{s/2}\Phi_r Q^{1/2}}_{\mathrm{HS}}
\leq \norm{(I-\Delta)^{s/2}\Phi_r}_{\mathrm{op}}
\Tr(Q)^{1/2}$
gives the sufficient condition
$s < H_1(2\alpha-1)/\alpha$.
If $(I-\Delta)^{s/2} Q^{1/2}$ is itself Hilbert-Schmidt,
then $H^s$ regularity follows for all $\alpha > 1/2$.
\item \emph{Cylindrical noise.}  For $Q = I$, the
stochastic convolution belongs to $H^s(\R)$ only under the
corresponding Hilbert-Schmidt condition
\begin{equation}\label{eq:spatial_reg_cyl}
\int_0^t \int_\R (1+|\xi|^2)^s\, r^{2\alpha-2}\,
|E_{\alpha,\alpha}(-c_{H_1}|\xi|^{2H_1} r^\alpha)|^2\,
d\xi\, dr < \infty.
\end{equation}
Using the same substitution as in
\Cref{thm:existence}, this is guaranteed when
$s < H_1(2\alpha-1)/\alpha - 1/2$.  At $s = 0$ this
recovers the cylindrical-noise well-posedness threshold
$H_1 > \alpha/(2(2\alpha-1))$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Effective context]
\label{def:eff_context}
The effective context $C_{\mathrm{eff}}(N)$ is the
maximum temporal depth at which stored information
remains above threshold $\varepsilon > 0$:
$C_{\mathrm{eff}}(N) := \sup\{\tau > 0 :
\exists\, k \leq N \text{ with }
|E_\alpha(-\lambda_k \tau^\alpha)| > \varepsilon\}$,
where $\lambda_k = c_{H_1}|\xi_k|^{2H_1}$ for
$N$ uniformly spaced modes
$\xi_k = k\Xi/N$, $k = 1, \ldots, N$ (excluding the
zero mode, which has $\lambda(0) = 0$ and would not

\label{thm:discretization}
Consider the fractional memory
process~\eqref{eq:quijotic_main} with impulse forcing
at times $s_1 < \cdots < s_M < t$:
\[
\dot{B}_t = \sum_{j=1}^M v^{(j)}\,\delta(t - s_j),
\qquad v^{(j)} \in L^2(\R).
\]
Then the mild solution at time $t > s_M$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:mild_impulse}
X_t = S_t f + \sum_{j=1}^M \Phi_{t-s_j}\, v^{(j)},

and its Fourier projection onto mode $\xi_k$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:discrete_exact}
\hat{X}_t(\xi_k)
= E_\alpha(-\lambda_k\,t^\alpha)\,\hat{f}(\xi_k)
+ \sum_{j=1}^M
(t - s_j)^{\alpha-1}\,
E_{\alpha,\alpha}\bigl(-\lambda_k\,(t - s_j)^\alpha\bigr)\,
\hat{v}^{(j)}(\xi_k),
\end{equation}
where $\lambda_k = c_{H_1}|\xi_k|^{2H_1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[$L^1$ integrability separates the
two representations]
\label{cor:l1_separation}
Fix $\lambda > 0$ and consider the scalar kernels on
$[0, \infty)$:
\[
G_{\mathrm{forced}}(\tau) := \tau^{\alpha-1}
E_{\alpha,\alpha}(-\lambda \tau^\alpha),
\qquad
G_{\mathrm{auto}}(\tau) := E_\alpha(-\lambda \tau^\alpha).
\]
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
\item For $\alpha \in (0, 1]$,
  $G_{\mathrm{forced}} \geq 0$ and
  $\int_0^\infty G_{\mathrm{forced}}(\tau)\,d\tau
  = 1/\lambda$.  For $\alpha \in (1, 2)$,
  $\|G_{\mathrm{forced}}\|_{L^1([0,\infty))}
  < \infty$.
\item For $\alpha \in (0, 1)$,
  $G_{\mathrm{auto}} \notin L^1([0, \infty))$: the
  integral $\int_0^\infty E_\alpha(-\lambda \tau^\alpha)
  \,d\tau$ diverges at infinity.  For $\alpha = 1$,
  $G_{\mathrm{auto}} = e^{-\lambda \tau}$ with
  $L^1$ norm $1/\lambda$.  For $\alpha \in (1, 2)$,
  $G_{\mathrm{auto}} \in L^1([0, \infty))$.
\end{enumerate}
The $L^1$ integrability transition of
$G_{\mathrm{auto}}$ occurs at $\alpha = 1$, coinciding
with the Markov-fractional boundary.
\end{corollary}

statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Retention boundary scaling]
\label{thm:retention}
Let $w_{\mathrm{exp}}(t) = e^{-\lambda t}$,
$w_{\mathrm{frac}}(t) = E_\alpha(-\lambda t^\alpha)$
with $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, $\lambda > 0$, and
$w_{\mathrm{power}}(t) = (1+t)^{-\beta}$ with
$\beta > 0$.  Assume $r_c > r_d$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textnormal{(Exponential, linear in
  $\lambda^{-1}$.)}  The retention boundary of the
  exponential kernel is given exactly by
  \[
  \tau^*_{\mathrm{exp}}(\lambda)
  \;=\; 1 + \frac{1}{\lambda}\,
    \ln\!\frac{r_c}{r_d}.
  \]

\item \textnormal{(Mittag-Leffler, polynomial in
  $\lambda^{-1}$ with exponent $1/\alpha$.)}  For
  $\lambda$ small enough that
  $\tau^*_{\mathrm{frac}}(\alpha, \lambda)$ lies in
  the asymptotic regime of $E_\alpha$, the retention
  boundary satisfies
  \[
  \tau^*_{\mathrm{frac}}(\alpha, \lambda)
  \;=\; \Bigl(\frac{r_c}
    {r_d\,w_{\mathrm{frac}}(1)\,\lambda\,
    \Gamma(1-\alpha)}\Bigr)^{1/\alpha}
    \,(1 + o(1)),
  \]
  so $\tau^*_{\mathrm{frac}}$ grows as
  $\lambda^{-1/\alpha}$ for fixed $\alpha$, and
  $\tau^*_{\mathrm{frac}}(\alpha, \lambda) \to
  \infty$ as $\alpha \to 0$ for any fixed $\lambda$.

\item \textnormal{(Power-law, exponential in
  $\beta^{-1}$.)}  The retention boundary of the
  power-law kernel is given exactly by
  \[
  \tau^*_{\mathrm{power}}(\beta)
  \;=\; 2\,\Bigl(\frac{r_c}{r_d}\Bigr)^{1/\beta}
    - 1.
  \]
  In particular, $\tau^*_{\mathrm{power}}(\beta) \to
  \infty$ as $\beta \to 0$, with growth exponential
  in $\beta^{-1}$ for $r_c > r_d$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
